audits.text:
## 6b1fe17a40a7

**Reproduced teaching shortcut — size rank is perfectly correlated with position
rank.** Audited `generator.py` SHA-256
`4a807878c53fd4d7124eeaa7294b924cd31afda5161950b299769c69d9c1abca`
without modifying it. Across 400 deterministic default draws (100 each for
None/easy/medium/hard), the four body objects always had sizes `[2,3,4,5]` in
ascending top-left position order. A rival that ignores size and assigns the
left-to-right/top-to-bottom objects to the row-0 marker colors therefore agrees
with every sampled generated lesson.

The authored counterexample has four row-0 markers and four separated connected
body objects of distinct sizes 2, 3, 4, and 5, but their position order has sizes
`[5,4,3,2]`. It passes the selected `self_check` and is accepted by
`arcpuzzles apply` as in-domain. The canonical Racket rule (`01b6bacad245`)
sorts by size and produces an output different from the position-order rival.
Full source-bound evidence is
`checks/audit/6b1fe17a40a7/counterexample.json`; the 400-draw census is
`checks/audit/6b1fe17a40a7/probe.json`, and the supported Racket receipt is
`checks/audit/6b1fe17a40a7/racket.json`.

The isolated audit preset likewise failed for a missing semantic contract and
found no selected task-local/frozen tests:
`checks/audit/6b1fe17a40a7-combined/`. Suggested future repair: randomize body
shapes and positions independently of size, include position/reading-order
rivals, and add a lesson contract requiring at least one demonstration where
size order differs from position order. This audit is findings-only; the source
was left unchanged.
